title: openai: /v1/chat.completions parity: roles, stop/logprobs, streaming stability, and response formatting
author: Ava Patel
release_notes: Enhances OpenAI /v1/chat.completions compatibility: correct role mapping, stable streaming framing, improved function-calling semantics, stop/logprobs support, and response formatting fixes. Backwards-compatible for existing Redwood API but recommend validating client streaming consumers due to improved chunk framing.
body: Summary: This PR brings the Redwood OpenAI-compat layer closer to parity with OpenAI's /v1/chat.completions endpoint. It addresses several API-surface differences observed in integration tests and customer reports: (1) strict role mapping (user/system/assistant), (2) correct handling of `stop` sequences including multi-token stops and partial-token streaming boundaries, (3) `logprobs` passthrough and deterministic token-index mapping, (4) structured response formatting improvements when `response_format` / `format` options are used, (5) function/tool-calling stability tweaks, and (6) streaming stability and chunk framing fixes so incremental JSON consumers receive valid partial payloads. Motivation: Multiple internal customers and the OpenAI-compat test-suite flagged discrepancies that cause downstream client failures (malformed JSON on stream reconnect, mis-mapped roles in chat history, incorrect stop truncation in streaming responses). This causes both UX regressions and eval flakiness. Design/Changes: - src/openai_compat/chat_handler.py: canonical mapping between Redwood message objects and OpenAI roles. New validation rejects unknown roles and normalizes 'system'/'assistant'/'user'. - src/runtime/streaming.py: reworked framing layer that guarantees each data: chunk emitted contains a complete UTF-8 token boundary and atomically-updated partial JSON envelope for the `delta` object. Added buffering for multi-byte tokens crossing chunk boundaries and logic to emit `data: [DONE]` only after KV cache flush. - src/serve/response_formatter.py: added formatting hooks for structured outputs; supports both OpenAI-style `choices[].message` and Redwood's richer `structured` output via content-type hints. - src/openai_compat/function_call.py: clarified function-calling semantics: prefer `name`-first matching for function selection, include `arguments` as JSON string in `choices[].message.function_call`, and fix a bug where `tool` fields were dropped during retries. - stop/logprobs: Implemented streaming-aware stop detection which checks both token-level sequences and string-level boundaries using a sliding-window buffer; `logprobs` are now attached to the same token indices as in OpenAI (token_index offset handling fixed). - Tests: comprehensive unit + e2e tests added under tests/test_chat_parity.py and integration tests exercising streaming reconnection and function calls. Backwards compatibility: The API surface is backward-compatible for typical Redwood users. The only client-visible change is more consistent streaming chunk framing and stricter role validation which will surface previously-silent malformed inputs (we document this). Rollout plan: staged canary on Dedicated (10% traffic) -> full rollout for Hosted API after 48h smoke and regression signals. Related work: ENG-2745 (OpenAI compat backlog), ENG-2791 (streaming stability initiative). Checklist: - [x] Role mapping implemented and unit-tested - [x] Streaming framing and partial-JSON invariants - [x] Stop sequence parity (multi-token) - [x] logprobs token index parity - [x] Function calling semantics and retries fixed - [x] Docs updated (openai_compat.md) - [x] Integration + e2e tests - [x] Canary/rollback wiring (console flags) Testing notes: run `pytest tests/test_chat_parity.py::TestChatParity` for unit scenarios, and `scripts/run_streaming_e2e.sh` for the end-to-end streaming reconnect tests. CI: initial integration run failed on e2e due to flakey test harness; after stabilizing the harness all checks passed. Known limitations: - Very large stop lists (>100 items) are handled but will be suggested to be client-side filtered for perf. - In rare high-throughput scenarios we may re-evaluate buffer sizing to reduce latency. Documentation: docs/openai_compat.md has an expanded section describing mapping and streaming differences.
